entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pseudo-Marius, a man claiming Gaius Marius the Younger's lineage, was a figure of intrigue in the tumultuous era following Julius Caesar's assassination. His alleged familial ties to the prominent Roman general garnered attention, as his murder on Mark Antony's orders exemplified the treacherous landscape of late Republic politics.

Pseudo-Marius's impact on historical records is often overshadowed by the prominent figures of his time, but his actions illustrate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the late Roman Republic.

The consequences of Pseudo-Marius's murder, however, had a lasting impact on the power dynamics of the time. His killing served as a stark reminder of the ruthless nature of the struggle for power that would soon engulf Rome.

The legacy of Pseudo-Marius's murder can be seen in the subsequent power struggles between Mark Antony and Octavian, ultimately shaping the course of Roman history.

'An act of treachery, a spark that ignited a flame of civil war.'
